ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.proof_nl:
Fix an integer n>1 and a real number t with (n-1)/n <= t < 1. Let k be any integer with 1 <= k <= n.

From t >= (n-1)/n, multiplying by the positive integer k gives
kt >= k(n-1)/n = k - k/n.
Because k <= n, we have k/n <= 1, so k - k/n >= k - 1. Hence kt >= k - 1.

Also, since t < 1 and k > 0, multiplying by k yields kt < k.

Therefore k - 1 <= kt < k. Since k - 1 is an integer, the definition of the floor function implies
floor(kt) = k - 1.

This holds for every integer k with 1 <= k <= n, as required.

result_payload.reason: The proof correctly establishes that for any integer k with 1 <= k <= n and any t in [(n-1)/n, 1), one has k-1 <= kt < k, hence floor(k*t)=k-1. The quantifiers match the lemma statement and there is no semantic drift.
